lines.speaker: pritchard
lines.text: Four one one seven is a page in a book. Silas keeps one for the town and one for himself. I've known it twenty years and never asked, for the town one always came out in our favour. I can write a warrant. My hand will manage that much.

lines.speaker: pritchard
lines.text: Then I arrest a man who has sat at my table every Sunday since my wife died, and the town goes hungry by Christmas because nobody else knows where anything is. And I'll do it. Don't look at my hand. I'll do it.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Good day. If it is on the shelf it is for sale, and if it is not, give me a week.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Four one one seven. Yes. I wondered who would come and say it. Sit down; you are letting the damp in. You have questions and I have a supper to carve at six, so let us be efficient.

buttons.label: I hear you keep two books.
Where does the silver come from?

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Four one one seven. And it is you who brings it. Good. I had hoped it would be somebody who has counted money on the Tellico road. Sit down. I have a supper to carve at six, so let us be efficient.

buttons.label: I hear you keep two books.
Where does the silver come from?

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Every merchant keeps two: the book that says what happened and the book that says what he wishes had. You may see the first for nothing. For the second, bring Owen and a paper, or come when I am not looking. I should respect either.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: You took a share on that road; Reese Dunmore itemises. So you know what a thing costs. Here. Turn it to the light. Six years, four columns, and not one army in this valley. Read it, and then tell me my price was too high.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: From people who want what I want, for reasons I have been careful never to learn. That is not evasion. It is the only honest answer I shall give you today, so do write it down.

lines.speaker: vickers
lines.text: Mr Vane is engaged. I can take a message, if it is brief and adds up.

lines.speaker: vickers
lines.text: You have misread the fourth column; that is a seven. Put the book down. I have kept it eleven years and it has never left this room. There are two barrels in this box. I would rather not spoil the carpet. It is his favourite.

buttons.label: He left you everything. Himself, nothing.

lines.speaker: vickers
lines.text: ...You have read the will. He never said. He never says anything that is not a number. Take it. Take it before I recollect myself. And if they hurt him I shall find you, and I am very thorough.

lines.speaker: vickers
lines.text: No. I am sorry. One. Two.

lines.speaker: vickers
lines.text: A hand. From the car door, at twenty past two, every fourth Thursday. A grey glove with a small square stitched on the cuff. It has never spoken. I sign; it withdraws. I have always thought it a very well-kept glove.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Listen to them. Six years I kept the Dominion's gate out of this street with a pencil, and Belden's list, and Clara's friends. They will hang me before supper for it. You have read it. You are the only one out here who has. What am I?

buttons.label: (Read the book out from the porch)
Sign it over. They never hear the rest.

lines.speaker: pritchard
lines.text: Stay behind me. ...That's Tolly Granger with the rope. I taught his boy to fish. Forty of them and I know every name, and my hand's doing what it does. If I draw I'll drop it. If I don't they go through me. Say something. Anything.

lines.speaker: granger
lines.text: Don't look at me like that. I printed his handbills! BEWARE THE ROADS, he had me set, forty point, and all the while he was paying to make it so! My sister's boy was on the fever list. I've a right. We've all a right.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: I hauled his sealed boxes three years and never opened one. So put me on the rope beside him, if that's what we're doing. No? Then somebody think what we ARE doing, and say it out loud, before that rope goes over.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Every page. Even the receipts for the school roof. That was fair. Nobody has been fair to me in some time, and I find I do not care for it. They will not hang me now. They will only never buy from me again. You have been very cruel.

buttons.label: Where does the silver come from?

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: There. Rail, river, mine. Released. And they go home believing it was an error in the accounts. So now there are two of us who know what quiet costs, and only one of us chose it. Welcome to the trade.

buttons.label: Where does the silver come from?

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Yours. How novel. Then your first report, employer: the silver comes by the night freight, sealed, from Blackstone Station. I have never been up that line. Nobody has, and come back to say so. I take it that is where you are going.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Blackstone Station. Up the dead line, past the Junction, where the night freight comes from and goes back to. That is all I know, and I have paid a great deal not to know more. If you go, go armed. And do give them my regards.

lines.speaker: pritchard
lines.text: I didn't draw. Twenty years of Sundays, and I stood on his steps and I did not draw. ...You stepped aside. I saw you. I'm not blaming you. I'd only like to know which of the two of us I'm going to be thinking about.

lines.speaker: haskell
lines.text: Received in good order, or not. I can tell you which. I cannot tell you why.

lines.speaker: haskell
lines.text: I sign for what arrives. That is all I do. But if somebody were to ask me a direct question, such as: Corwin, did you ever weigh one of Mr Vane's sealed crates... I should have to answer. Nobody has ever asked.

buttons.label: Corwin. Did you ever weigh one?

lines.speaker: haskell
lines.text: Ninety-one pounds. Entered as dry goods, eleven pounds. I wrote it down. It is in the lining of the receiving book. They come off the night freight from past Iron Junction. From Blackstone. There. I have wanted to say that for a year.

lines.speaker: haskell
lines.text: They've burned the post. The book's gone with it. But I kept a page. I always keep a page. The crates came from Blackstone Station. Take it. Somebody ought to have asked me sooner. I ought to have said without asking.
